title: Reading the Word
definition: Reading the Word is the regular practice of receiving Scripture with attention, humility, and faith.
summary: Reading the Word is the regular practice of receiving Scripture with attention, humility, and faith.
christFocus: Jesus calls His people to hear and keep God’s Word, and regular reading brings believers again and again to the truth of who He is and how to follow Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Reading the Word is one of the simplest and most important ways believers receive God’s truth. It does not require a platform, degree, or perfect life. It requires a heart willing to listen to God.

Regular Scripture reading forms the believer over time. Some days may feel powerful; other days may feel ordinary. Yet the Word continues to expose, comfort, instruct, warn, and guide. God often grows His people through steady faithfulness rather than dramatic moments.

Reading Scripture brings us to Christ. The Bible reveals His person, His work, His promises, His commands, and His heart for sinners and sufferers. A believer who reads the Word is learning to listen to the Shepherd.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many believers wait until they feel spiritual enough to read Scripture. The Word is not only for strong days; it is also for weak days, confused days, grieving days, and recovering days.

This doctrine corrects the idea that Bible reading is a religious box to check. Reading the Word is communion with the God who speaks and discipleship under the Lord who leads.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Begin with a manageable portion of Scripture and read with prayer. Do not despise small beginnings. Ask what the passage reveals about God, Christ, sin, grace, obedience, and hope, then respond with one faithful step.
